title: Etale atlas and finite descent for nodal trait normalization
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring, $\pi$ a uniformizer, $K$ its fraction field, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:X	o S$ be projective, flat and finitely presented [def-kun-projective, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Assume its geometric fibres are nonempty reduced curves of pure dimension one, and each nonsmooth closed point over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Then $X$ is Noetherian and reduced. Write $
u:C=X^
u	o X$ for its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. There is a jointly surjective finite family of affine etale morphisms $U_a	o X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] with the following descriptions of $C	imes_XU_a	o U_a$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. A chart meeting the special fibre has an etale map $U_a	o\operatorname{Spec}Q_a$ over an etale DVR extension $R	o R_a$ with uniformizer $\pi_a$, where $Q_a=R_a[u,v]/(uv)$ or $R_a[u,v]/(uv-\pi_a^n)$, $n\geq0$. In the first case its normalization is the pullback of $\operatorname{Spec}(R_a[u]	imes R_a[v])	o\operatorname{Spec}Q_a$; in the second it is the identity. The remaining charts lie over $K$ and are smooth charts with identity normalization, or etale over $K_a[u,v]/(uv)$ for a finite separable field extension $K_a/K$, with the same two-branch normalization formula. Polynomial rings use [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Moreover $
u$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], $C	o S$ is projective, flat and finitely presented with nonempty nodal geometric fibres in the stated sense, and $C_K$ is smooth. Normalization restricts to the identity on the relative smooth locus of $X$, and $C_K	o X_K$ is the componentwise normalization of $X_K$. No excellence or completeness assumption on $R$ is made.

proof.text: A DVR is Noetherian: each nonzero ideal is generated by a power of its uniformizer. Thus $S$ is Noetherian. Finite presentation implies finite type directly from the affine presentation and quasi-compactness. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $f$ to obtain Noetherian $X$. The geometric generic fibre is reduced by hypothesis, so [lem-trf-geometric-reducedness-algebraic-closure-test], applied over $K$, implies that $X_K$ itself is reduced. For an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] makes $B$ flat over $R$, and [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain] makes multiplication by each $\pi^m$ injective. Hence $B\to B[1/\pi]$ is injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the latter ring is the ring of the open $V_K$ of $X_K$, so is reduced. A nilpotent in $B$ therefore maps to zero and is zero. The affine cover proves that $X$ is reduced. Finally, every nonsmooth point of every geometric fibre $X_\Omega$ is closed. A nonclosed point of a reduced pure one-dimensional $X_\Omega$ is the generic point of an irreducible component, since a proper specialization chain has length at most one. Cover $X_\Omega$ by the affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega\otimes_RA)$ of finite-presentation charts $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$; they are finitely presented and flat over the field $\Omega$, Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and their geometric fibre over $\Omega=\bar\Omega$ is the chart itself, hence reduced. So [lem-trf-generic-fibre-points-smooth] makes these generic points smooth. Thus the completed-local-ring condition of the hypothesis holds at all nonsmooth geometric-fibre points, which is the form required by [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-local-model] and [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-source-locality].

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); varieties.tex Tag 035X (lemma-geometrically-reduced); agent torsion-free injection argument

proof.text: For every point of the special fibre use [lem-sfb-dvr-nodal-etale-local-form]. Its flatness, local finite presentation and geometric nodal hypotheses are precisely those assumed here; projectivity is not needed for this application. It supplies the common etale neighbourhood and the two equations in the statement, with no excellence hypothesis. Replace the neighbourhood by an affine open containing its distinguished point; both maps remain etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The map to the affine model is then a finite-type map between affines: it is locally of finite presentation, and affine maps are quasi-compact. Thus this affine neighbourhood is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian].

Cover the relative smooth locus of $X_K$ by affine open smooth $K$-schemes. For every remaining point apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-local-model] to $X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, whose geometric fibres are those of $X$ over the generic point, so its all-points nodal hypothesis holds by step 1, obtaining $U\to W$ over an etale $V\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], shrink $V$ at the chosen point to $\operatorname{Spec}K_a$ for a finite separable extension $K_a/K$, and restrict $U$ accordingly. The parameter $h$ of the model must vanish: [lem-trf-nodal-model-etale-smooth-locus] puts the chosen point in $V(u,v)$, hence $h=uv=0$ in the field $K_a$. Thus $W=\operatorname{Spec}K_a[u,v]/(uv)$. Restrict $U$ further to an affine neighbourhood of its point. These maps, including their composites into $X$, are etale: $X_K\hookrightarrow X$ is the inverse image of $D(\pi)$, an open immersion, and open immersions and composites are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The new affine charts are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian].

The images of the affine etale charts of steps 2--3 are open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], and they cover every point of $X$. Since $X$ is quasi-compact by step 1, choose finitely many of these images covering $X$, retaining their charts. Their disjoint union $T=\coprod_aU_a\to X$ is surjective and flat by the definition of etale and [def-weil-flat-morphism]. It is quasi-compact: each $U_a$ is Noetherian, so the inverse image in it of any quasi-compact open of $X$ is an open subset of a Noetherian space and is quasi-compact; only finitely many $a$ occur. Thus this is an fpqc cover. We will use precisely this same finite atlas for every normalization description.

proof.text:
Let $
u:C=X^
u	o X$ be the componentwise normalization. By [lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-generic-properties], it is integral and surjective. For every retained chart $U_a	o X$, [lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-smooth-pullback] identifies $C	imes_XU_a$ with $U_a^
u$ over $U_a$. For every model chart $U_a	o\operatorname{Spec}Q_a$, the same result identifies $U_a^
u$ with $U_a	imes_{\operatorname{Spec}Q_a}(\operatorname{Spec}Q_a)^
u$. Both applications are legitimate: $X$, $U_a$, and the polynomial quotient models are locally Noetherian, and the maps are etale, hence smooth. This comparison does not presuppose finite normalization.

For a zero-parameter model over the DVR $R_a$ or field $K_a$, apply [lem-sfb-split-node-normalization-conductor] with that coefficient ring. It states exactly that its normalization algebra is $E=R_a[u]\times R_a[v]$ (respectively $K_a[u]\times K_a[v]$), via the two axis restrictions, and that $E$ is finite over $Q_a$. Thus step 5 gives the asserted two-branch pullback formula. It also says that the two branches are smooth over the coefficient ring. The pulled normalization is etale over their disjoint union, since its map is the base change of $U_a\to\operatorname{Spec}Q_a$, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits].

For $Q_a=R_a[u,v]/(uv-\pi_a^n)$, including $n=0$, the nonzero-parameter normal-domain clause of [lem-sfb-binomial-laurent-normal-form] applies to the normal domain $R_a$ and $a=\pi_a^n$. It says that $Q_a$ and every prime localization are normal domains. A DVR is a normal domain: the valuation of an integral element of its fraction field cannot be negative, since in a monic equation its highest power would have strictly least valuation. Consequently [lem-sfb-split-node-normalization-conductor], normal-domain clause, makes the normalization of $\operatorname{Spec}Q_a$ the identity. Step 5 then makes $C\times_XU_a\to U_a$ the identity. There is no requirement $n=1$, and no appeal to normality of completion.

If $W$ is any locally Noetherian normal scheme, apply [lem-sfb-integral-normal-generic-recognition] to $\operatorname{id}_W$: it is integral, its generic points correspond identically, and the residue-field maps are identities. This identifies $W^\nu\to W$ with the identity. Apply this observation first to each affine smooth generic chart. Its local rings are normal by [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent], since a field is normal. Apply it also to the relative smooth locus of $X$: all its local rings are integrally closed domains by [lem-sfb-smooth-trait-curve-local-properties]. The open restriction comparison of [lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-smooth-pullback] now proves that $\nu$ restricts to the identity on that whole locus. Its relative dimension is one by the pure-dimensional fibre hypothesis.

Each pullback of $\nu$ to $U_a$ is finite: it is an identity in steps 7--8, and is the pullback of a finite algebra in step 6. For the latter assertion write $U_a=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]: its normalization has algebra $B\otimes_{Q_a}E$, generated over $B$ by the tensors of any finite $Q_a$-module generating set of $E$. This is a direct finite-generation calculation, using the definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The pullback to the finite disjoint union $T$ is therefore finite. Apply [lem-sbc-finite-morphism-fpqc-descent] with the flat, surjective, quasi-compact cover $T\to X$ of step 4. It proves that $\nu$ is finite. Surjectivity was already supplied in step 5.

Put $C_a=C\times_XU_a$. These schemes form a jointly surjective etale cover of $C$ by base change, using [lem-trf-etale-source-fibre-preparation] or the covering and base-change clause [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. If $C_a\to U_a$ is an identity, $C_a\to S$ is the family $X\to S$, nodal in the all-points sense by step 1, precomposed with an etale map, so [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-source-locality] gives nodality. For a separated-branch chart, step 6 makes $C_a$ etale over two affine lines over $R_a$ or $K_a$. Those affine lines are smooth with pure one-dimensional geometric fibres; they are smooth over the coefficient ring by [lem-sfb-split-node-normalization-conductor], hence locally finitely presented by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and flat because $R_a[u]$ is a free $R_a$-module, and have no nonsmooth fibre points. Source locality gives nodality over that coefficient ring, and [lem-sfb-scheme-nodal-etale-postcomposition] gives nodality over $S$, since both $\operatorname{Spec}R_a\to S$ and $\operatorname{Spec}K_a\to S$ are etale. Finally [lem-trf-nodal-family-etale-source-locality] for the cover $\{C_a\to C\}$ proves that $C\to S$ is flat and locally finitely presented with pure one-dimensional geometric fibres and only the stated nodal singularities.

The geometric fibres in step 10 are reduced as well. On an identity chart their etale maps to the original geometric fibre have reduced target by hypothesis, so [etale-proposition-etale-reduced] applies. On a separated-branch chart the fibre is smooth over its algebraically closed field (the branches are smooth, and etale maps and their composites are smooth); [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent] gives normal, hence reduced, local rings. To descend this to a point $c$ of the geometric fibre of $C$, choose a point $d$ above it on one of these covering charts. The stalk map $A=\mathcal O_{C_\Omega,c}\to B=\mathcal O_{(C_a)_\Omega,d}$ is flat and local by the definition of etale and [def-weil-flat-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] it is faithfully flat, and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] with the module $A$ says it is injective. A nilpotent of $A$ maps to zero in reduced $B$, so is zero. This supplies reducedness without treating an unproved completion comparison as descent.

On the generic fibre every chart of $C$ is smooth. The original smooth charts remain unchanged. The separated-branch charts are smooth by step 6 and smooth composition [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. For a nonzero-parameter special chart, invert $\pi_a$: the equation becomes $uv=a$ with $a\ne0$ over $\operatorname{Frac}R_a$, and [lem-sfb-binomial-geometric-fibres] says this hyperbola is smooth. Its etale pullback is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] and smooth composition. The field $\operatorname{Frac}R_a/K$ is finite separable, by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] applied to $\operatorname{Spec}R_a\to S$ at the generic point, and $\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}R_a\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is etale, being the base change of the etale $\operatorname{Spec}R_a\to S$ along $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits], hence smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]; so composing its structure map to $K$ preserves smoothness. Apply [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness] to the resulting etale cover of $C_K$ to conclude $C_K$ is smooth. Finally apply [lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-smooth-pullback] to the open immersion $X_K\hookrightarrow X$: it identifies $C_K\to X_K$ with the componentwise normalization of $X_K$.

proof.text: Projectivity must be checked in the finite-projective-space convention of [def-kun-projective]. The hypothesis makes $X\to S$ projective also in the projective-bundle convention, using the free module defining $\mathbf P^N_S$ [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. By [lem-trf-finite-projective-bundle], finite $\nu$ is projective in that bundle convention, and [lem-sfb-projective-bundle-composition] makes $C\to S$ projective in the same convention; the affine trait $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Its structure sheaf is ample directly by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]: take $n=1$, section $1$, and $S_1=S$ at every point. Therefore [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] converts $C\to S$ to the required finite-projective-space embedding. It is of finite type by [lem-sfb-projective-bundle-relative-ample], hence quasi-compact; it is quasi-separated since it embeds as a closed subscheme of a separated projective space. Together with local finite presentation from step 10, this is finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

Surjectivity of $\nu$ in step 5 persists on geometric fibres: if $x$ is a point of $X_\Omega$ over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$, choose a point $c$ of $C$ over its image in $X$. The tensor product $\kappa(c)\otimes_{\kappa(x_0)}\kappa(x)$ of the two field extensions of $\kappa(x_0)$ is nonzero: bases of the two vector spaces give a basis of their tensor product containing $1\otimes1$. It has a prime ideal, whose point is a lift in $C\times_XX_\Omega=C_\Omega$, by the affine fibre-product description [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Thus $C_\Omega\to X_\Omega$ is surjective. The hypothesized nonempty geometric fibres of $X$ imply those of $C$ are nonempty. Together, steps 5--13 prove every claimed normalization, family and atlas assertion. None used excellence or completeness.
